title: ‘We’re not a criminal gang, just criminal friends’: Narrative ambiguity and identity performance in times of gang mood
abstract: Based on qualitative data from Norway, we examine how men labelled as gang members draw on multiple narrative resources to construct and contest meanings of self and social position during a time of heightened ‘gang talk’, which we refer to as gangmood. Building on scholarship highlighting the performative dimensions of gang identity and street codes, we foreground the role of ambiguity in narrative practice as a response to asymmetry, showing how ambiguous stories generate new layers of interpretation, adjustment and negotiation, making gang identity not a fixed status, but an ongoing and situated process. Ambiguity, then, should not be seen as simply a lack of clarity or stable selfhood, but as a mechanism through which selves are made and remade across situations and audiences.
